cn_m10: A batch of 34 surplus American M10 tank destroyers was bought by the Kuomintang in 1948 and taken to Taiwan without fighting on the mainland; some were later rebuilt with Japanese 105 mm howitzers as makeshift artillery until the M7 Priest took over in the mid-1950s. In the game it matches the US M10 except that it cannot fit the add-on armour. The gun hits hard, but the turret turns very slowly, mobility is modest and the open roof leaves the crew exposed to HE and artillery, so it works best from ambush. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m113a1_tow: Taiwan bought 634 M113A1 carriers in the mid-1960s and later armed some Marine Corps examples with American TOW missiles on an Israeli-made RAMTA launcher; Humvees have since inherited that role. With only the missile launcher and a machine gun, it belongs well behind the front line. The missiles defeat anything without ERA or an active protection system, and the tall launcher with 20 degrees of depression can fire over even steep crests while the hull stays hidden. The catch is the launcher itself, which is exposed and fragile, and it can only swing through a narrow arc. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m18_hellcat: The 76 mm M18 was the first combat vehicle the United States handed to the Republic of China under Korean War-era aid, arriving from 1952; 243 were delivered and they stayed in service into the 1970s, some ending up as fixed coastal guns. Speed is its main asset in the game, getting it to flanks and key positions early, where the M1 gun's APCBC shot can deal with most opponents. With thin armour and an open turret, though, almost any return fire is dangerous. It was added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m1a2t: Taiwan ordered 108 Abrams in 2018–2019 to replace its CM11 and M60A3 TTS fleets; the resulting M1A2T is derived from the M1A2 SEP V3 with a downgraded armour package, and at least 40 had been delivered by December 2024. It performs much like the American M1A2 SEP, suiting both aggressive and defensive play, and its strong thermal sight helps at long range and in bad weather. Like every Abrams it relies on terrain to cover a hull that even early APFSDS can defeat, and with no TUSK kit on offer, strong ATGMs are a greater threat. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
cn_m24_chaffee: A handful of M24 light tanks reached Nationalist China under wartime lend-lease, and 289 more followed to Taiwan in the 1950s as Korean War-era aid, receiving various upgrades as the design aged. In the game it mixes a hard-hitting gun with good speed and passable armour, a combination best used to grab flanking positions early rather than to slug it out with enemy tanks. It has been in the Chinese tree since Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m36: China's M36 story has two strands: the People's Volunteer Army captured one in Korea, now displayed in the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution, while Taiwan's army took ten ex-French M36B2s that duelled with PLA artillery during the First Taiwan Strait Crisis and served until the late 1970s. The in-game vehicle is a copy of the American M36 GMC with one difference: it has no access to the M304 APCR shot. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m3a3_stuart: The M3A3 refined the Stuart with a welded, sloped hull borrowed from the M5 line and a turret bustle for the radio. Nationalist China received 48 under lend-lease to form its first tank battalion in India, and many were later captured by the PLA, which kept them until the late 1950s. Its sloped plates are the main draw in the game, turning away some small-calibre rounds that would go through the fronts of other early light tanks, though that protection is no licence to trade shots. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m3a3_stuart_1st_ptg: This premium Stuart represents the Chinese-American 1st Provisional Tank Group, the lend-lease battalion formed in India that helped the Allies reopen the Ledo-Burma Road through Japanese-held Burma. In battle it is identical to the tech-tree M3A3, so its angled front plates give it an advantage over other early light tanks against small-calibre guns, but it is still too thinly armoured for slugging matches. It was added in the "Wind of Change" update.
cn_m41_a3_walker_bulldog: Taiwan's M41A3 was an M41A1 re-engined with a fuel-injected AOS 895-5 diesel, received from 1958 and used mainly for fire support on the outlying islands and for training until the last one retired in February 2022; 50 others were rebuilt as M41Ds. In the game it keeps the M41's excellent mobility and a gun that can defeat most WWII-era tanks when it catches them side-on, but it gives up the APDS and HEATFS rounds of other nations' versions in exchange for meeting weaker opposition. It suits careful flanking and joined the game in the "Sons of Attila" update.
cn_m42_duster: Taiwan's army and marines received the twin-40 mm M42 from 1958 to replace the M19; once supersonic jets made it outdated it was used mostly for fire support, a job it still occasionally does in exercises. The in-game version is identical to the American one. As an anti-aircraft vehicle it is considered weak, with a fully exposed crew and only 120 rounds per minute, and it lacks the armour to fight tanks openly, so survival depends on hugging cover and limiting exposure.
cn_m48a1_patton_III: Taiwan bought 309 ex-US Army M48A1s between 1973 and 1980 under Project Fire Bull to counter the PLA's Type 59s, and they formed the core of its armour until M60A3 TTS tanks arrived in the 1990s; 100 were later rebuilt with 105 mm guns as the CM12. In the game it behaves exactly like the American and Israeli M48A1. The 90 mm gun handles WWII-era tanks comfortably, but the tall, bulky hull is easy to spot and hit, so it is most useful in a supporting role. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a1_76w_sherman: Six of these hybrid Shermans reached Taiwan's army from Britain in late 1949: they had the cast M4A1 hull and large-mantlet turret of the M4A1 (76) W but carried the older 75 mm M3 gun, and were retired in 1952 once the M18 became the main tank. Hull-down is where it shines in the game: good gun depression lets it hide the weak-spotted M4A1 hull and show only a turret better armoured than those of the Shermans it usually meets. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a4_sherman: China received 32 M4A4 Shermans through lend-lease for the 1st Provisional Tank Group in India; after the war they fought in the civil war with the New First and New Sixth Armies until defeat in the Liaoshen Campaign. The M4A4's hull was stretched by 15 cm to fit the Chrysler multibank engine, itself built from five car engines. Experienced opponents will aim for its front hull, where the hatches bulge out of the slope and the welded-on extra plates only partly make up for it. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m4a4_sherman_1st_ptg: This premium M4A4 carries the markings of the 1st Provisional Tank Group, the lend-lease unit of the Chinese Expeditionary Forces that fought in the China-Burma-India theatre and helped reopen the Ledo-Burma Road. It is the tech-tree M4A4 with a unique camouflage and a roof-mounted M2HB, so it plays like other 75 mm Shermans, and its vertical stabiliser makes shooting on the move more practical. First sold as a pack with Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it was withdrawn after the 2021 May sale, briefly returned for China's National Day that year, and came back for Golden Eagles in the "Sky Guardians" update.
cn_m55: Six M55 self-propelled 203 mm howitzers were lent to Taiwan during the 1958 Second Taiwan Strait Crisis and posted to Kinmen, but reportedly went back to the US after just a week, partly over a friendly-fire incident, in exchange for static 8-inch guns. In the game everything rests on the howitzer, whose HE shell holds roughly 23 kg of TNT equivalent, enough to wreck any tank if placed well. With a ten-round load and a very slow reload, though, each miss is costly, and the large, thin-skinned hull rarely survives the reply. It was added in the "Tusk Force" update.
cn_m5a1_stuart: Nationalist China first got M5A1 Stuarts from the US in 1948; after heavy civil war losses, its armoured command bought tanks the Americans had left behind on Pacific islands, and one rebuilt battalion assembled 22 M5A1s from salvaged vehicles and parts. In the game it handles much like the M3A3 and other early American light tanks, built for scouting and supporting infantry rather than fighting enemy armour head-on. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m60a3_tts: Taiwan took 460 ex-US M60A3 TTS tanks, ordered in two batches in 1994 and 1996, to replace its ageing M48A1s, and they have served alongside the CM11 since; plans for a domestic 120 mm upgrade were dropped in favour of buying the M1A2T. In the game it brings thermal imaging, a stabiliser working in both planes, responsive gun handling and plenty of ammunition types. It is also a big target with little armour and unremarkable mobility, so its best results come from cover, where its fire control advantage tells. It was part of the Chinese ground tree from Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m8_greyhound: Ford's wartime M8 armoured car served with US and British forces from 1943; in 1949 a few were taken in mainland China, and others went to Taiwan's army, which used them for riot control rather than combat. In the game it is identical to the American M8, with a 37 mm gun and a rear-mounted M2HB that earns its keep against light armour and early aircraft. Aircraft are also its main danger, since strafing runs reach the crew through the open top. It came with Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m8_scott: Only small numbers of M8 HMCs reached Nationalist China through lend-lease, since Japanese control of the coast made deliveries difficult, and the type may have seen limited action in the Huai Hai campaign. The low-velocity 75 mm howitzer struggles at range, yet its arcing trajectory is also a tool: from behind a low obstacle it can drop shells onto enemies that cannot see it. An M2HB on the roof handles lightly armoured targets and early aircraft. It was introduced in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
cn_m_41d: The M41D was Taiwan's 1990s rebuild of 50 M41A1/A2 Walker Bulldogs, adding a domestic gun able to fire APFSDS, upgraded fire control and an easier-to-maintain engine. The most modern M41 in the game, it has a laser rangefinder, thermal sight and APFSDS but a weaker engine. It is a hull-down sniper: depression and rangefinder suit long shots from cover, poor armour and no stabiliser rule out much else, and brisk reversing gets it away when found. Next to China's PTL02 it reverses better, sits lower and depresses further, but lacks the stabiliser and some firepower. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
cn_mbt2000: NORINCO developed the MBT-2000 for Pakistan, where it is called the Al-Khalid, through the Type 90-II programme; it ended up with a Ukrainian 6TD power pack and was shown as an export product at IDEX 2001. That powertrain sets it apart from the Soviet-derived tanks around it in the Chinese tree, giving T-80UD-like forward speed, unusually quick reverse and neutral steering. The gun matches T-72 equivalents but with better fire control, while protection falls short of tanks like the ZTZ96A, so mobility is its main asset. It joined the game in the "Sons of Attila" update.
cn_mbt2000_sm: This is the MBT-2000, NORINCO's export tank for Pakistan (the Al-Khalid), in a special appearance themed on the character Lin for the 2026 Senrai Maidens event; otherwise it matches the standard version. It brings an autoloading 125 mm gun with modern fire control and a thermal sight, NERA composite armour topped with FY-2 ERA that copes with common APFSDS and HEAT, and a 6TD-2 engine that reverses far better than Soviet designs. The trade-offs are thin sides, ammunition sharing the crew compartment and restricted gun elevation.
cn_object_122tm: Object 122MT was a Chinese second-generation tank prototype of the late 1960s and 1970s, built at the Luoyang Tractor Factory against the Soviet threat and drawing on technology from a captured T-62; work stalled amid the upheaval of the Cultural Revolution and the vehicle remains stored at the factory. Nicknamed the "triple-mechanical" prototype in China, it combined what is described as the world's first 120 mm smoothbore gun with a turret-mounted ATGM, a laser rangefinder and a new diesel engine. It came to the game in the "Danger Zone" update.
cn_object_211: Object 211 was the PLA's late-1950s project for an amphibious tank suited to southern China's rivers and paddy fields, developed with the help of purchased PT-76s and leading to the Type 63; the game models the fourth prototype with the 85 mm Type 63 gun, now kept at Institute 201. It trades protection for pace: the hull barely keeps out machine-gun rounds and shell splinters, but it is low and fast enough to seize good positions at the start, and the 85 mm gun punishes anything it hits squarely. It was added in the "La Royale" update.
cn_oplot_t: Ukraine's T-84 grew out of the T-80UD with a welded turret, and the Oplot-M is its latest production model; Pakistan evaluated it against the VT-4 in 2015–2017 but chose the Chinese tank. In the game it can reverse at 32 km/h, quicker than any other Eastern Bloc design, and its three crew sit behind ERA and NERA with an electrical APS on top. The gun is the weak part, underpowered and short of depression, and gaps such as the one between skirts and hull give opponents targets. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead" and matches the Thai Oplot-T in Japan's tree.
cn_pgz_04a: The PGZ04A upgrades the PLA's PGZ95 gun-missile SPAA, which grew out of a 1980s requirement shaped by the Italian SIDAM 25, fitting newer MANPADS for the army's close-range air defence layer. In the game it combines four 25 mm cannons, derived from the Shilka's guns but slower-firing with higher velocity and penetration, with a search radar and thermal optics. The missiles are the reason to take it: four HN-6s, a touch better than Stingers, reach aircraft well beyond gun range, making up for electronics, mobility and ground-attack ability that fall short of the newer PGZ09. It came with the "Red Skies" update.
cn_pgz_09: The PGZ09 has defended PLA ground forces since the late 2000s, its 35 mm guns tracing back to the licence-built Oerlikon KDA; the production version dropped the infrared missiles planned for the turret. The game positions it as China's counterpart to the Gepard and Type 87, aimed at helicopters, drones and cruise missiles. It finds and follows targets with its own search and tracking radars, backed by an electro-optical system and second-generation thermals, then engages with 35 mm AHEAD shells that are dangerous to aircraft and unwary ground vehicles; good off-road speed keeps it with the advance. It was introduced in the "Red Skies" update.
cn_pgz_625_fb10: NORINCO's CS/SA5 (Type 625E) pairs a rotary cannon with short-range missiles in a module on a modified ZBL-08 8x8 chassis, aimed at low-flying aircraft, helicopters and drones; it was unveiled at Zhuhai in 2016 and entered service in 2022. Whether used as a dedicated air-defence picket or as a second-line vehicle supporting tanks with its cannon, it has to husband its ammunition and avoid return fire, being large and thinly armoured. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
cn_pgz_88: Inspired by the ZSU-23-4's success in 1973, the PGZ88 mounted two 37 mm Type 65 guns and a radar fire control system on a Type 79 tank chassis; unresolved problems limited orders to 24, which now serve the PLA only for training. Its guns fire quickly and their HE shells carry a heavy explosive charge, so aircraft go down fast, while the AP rounds have enough penetration to threaten tanks. Autocannons go straight through its armour, and comparable vehicles generally outpace it. It came with Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
cn_plz_05: The PLZ05 is the PLA's tracked 155 mm self-propelled howitzer, in service since the early 2000s; it refined the export PLZ45 with a 2S19-derived autoloader, a longer L/52 barrel and a stronger engine. Like the VIDAR, Type 99 and PzH 2000, it puts a fast-firing, high-velocity gun on a tall, lightly armoured hull with sluggish gun handling, and its HE is somewhat weaker than NATO 155 mm rounds. What it adds is a laser rangefinder, a SAP shell for flank shots, a ready rack holding all 30 rounds, spall liners and adjustable suspension that improves effective depression. It arrived in the "Firebirds" update.
